## Why

S0 findings F-097/F-131 (RI-01): camera-registry source ids were
minted from personal ArcGIS **account handles** (and one id from a
surname) and leak into every public identifier surface — source,
target, subject, claim and permalink ids, tile properties, registry
non-id text (41 e-mail-shaped owner strings and handle tokens), and
one `camera_operator` claim value. The claim spine is append-only
(SIG-STORE-011), so the recorded claims keep the strings; what had to
change is what the *public* surface carries.

Operator answers honoured (verbatim in ADR-178):

- **DR-C6-01 [B-3]** — "Re-key, map restricted (Recommended)":
  neutral ids; old URLs answer a neutral "identifier changed" page;
  the old→new map stays restricted (a public redirect would republish
  the handles); the re-keyed pages ride P34.21b's republish #2.
- **A-0.1 [OD-17]** — "No, wait for P34.18": the 41 e-mail-shaped
  owner strings and handle tokens are removed from registry non-id
  text on this branch now; public `main` changes only on the
  operator's merge.
- **A-0.4 [OD-20]** — "Accept and disclose (Recommended)": git
  history keeps the strings (agents never rewrite history); the dated
  correction note discloses it.

## What this does

- **ADR-178** lands with the three operator answers quoted verbatim
  (rounds + receipt times), the neutral-id rule, append-only alias
  semantics, the restricted-map location and readership, the
  no-redirect old-URL rule, the disclosed-history posture, the plain
  sha256-vs-HMAC trade-off recorded, and `## Revisit trigger`.
  ADR-137 and ADR-169 carry appended status notes for the strings the
  re-key redacted inside their bodies (landed bodies otherwise
  untouched).
- **Registry re-key at the repo tip** —
  `sig-connectors rekey-personal-ids` (dry-run default, `--apply`;
  committed, idempotent — a re-run restores the plan from the prior
  restricted map and changes nothing). It reads the handle list only
  from the gitignored
  `docs/build/logs/next-phase/C3/personal_like_ids.txt`, never prints
  a handle (all reports are counts only), rewrites `sources.toml`,
  `camera_registry_targets.toml`, `live_targets.toml` and every
  tracked file carrying a handle-list token, `git mv`s the 32
  rights-annex paths, and scrubs the non-id owner/agency/notes text.
  Apply result: 32 source ids + 32 target ids re-keyed to
  deterministic neutral ids (`camreg_us_ny_<n>`, `camreg_und_<n>`,
  `okc_council_statement`), 4 compound-token classes, 96 files, 545
  occurrences, 190 suppressed-value digests, 0 leftovers.
- **Alias resolution without a public list** —
  `policy/src/policy/data/source_aliases.json` carries `sha256:`
  digests of retired tokens only (source, target, compound, phrase,
  redaction and suppressed-value classes); the plaintext map lives
  only at the gitignored
  `docs/build/logs/p34.18/restricted_source_map.json` (mode 0600)
  and, on the hosted leg, the `sig-restricted` object — its sha256 is
  in the committed table as the audit anchor. `policy.source_aliases`
  is the single resolver; unknown values pass through.
- **Every public field (TS-04)** — the projection runs at the seams:
  `exports.shaping` (claim/subject/source ids, value text, raw values,
  attribution), `exports.spine_export` (supplementary tables +
  materialized graph data via a recursive `resolve_public_text`),
  `resolution.camera_sites_pg` (site subjects/sources/targets/claims/
  external refs), the API `IdentifierAliasMiddleware` (bounded
  response-body projection across JSON, JSON-LD, HTML and Turtle),
  and the web build (`web/src/lib/{alias,sources}.ts`).
  `camera_operator` values digesting onto the suppressed set are
  marked non-publishable in shaping and dropped to `None` in the
  materialization — the recorded claim stays in the spine; the full
  predicate fix stays P35.26's.
- **Old URLs answer N-5, never a redirect** —
  `web/src/pages/sources/identifier-changed.astro` ("This identifier
  has changed.", `4f628b89a266`, `data-notice="N-5"`, noindex) is
  served in place by the generated `conf/renamed_*.conf` exact-match
  barrier included from `ops/web/nginx.conf`; `sig-ops renamed-routes`
  builds it from the restricted map. A 301 would publish the mapping
  and repeat the handle — that is what B-3 forbade. The page ships
  with P34.21b's republish #2, not this branch's publish.
- **Correction note** — `docs/governance/identifier-rekey-note.md`
  (dated): which identifiers changed, why (personal data, Part VIII),
  that old citations resolve to the neutral notice, and that git
  history retains the old strings (OD-20 — the disclosure condition
  for P37.55's deposits). Governance README updated ten→eleven
  documents. The N-5 sentence is a `pending` sha256 row in copy
  batch #2 (`docs/build/reports/copy-batches/batch-02.md`).
- **Crawl check** — `docs/build/tools/handle_crawl_check.py` scans a
  build tree, an export tree, tiles and the repo tip for any
  handle-list entry in every TS-04 field, reporting counts only and
  skipping with a recorded reason when the handle list is absent.
  On this tree: **pass — 0 hits** (functional 0/0, other 0/0,
  retained 0/0). P34.47 runs it live.
- **Consistency landings** — ADR-178 in Appendix F via
  `spec_src/99a_appF_adr.md` → `BUILD.sh` (byte-identical);
  `ADR_TRIGGERS.csv` register row (home BL-084); BL-084 `sources` +
  regenerated `BACKLOG.md`; appended status notes on ADR-137/169; the
  `p32.23a` CANDIDATE_MANIFEST byte_size/sha256 re-pointed at the
  re-keyed artifact (targeted edit, never a falsified digest).
